meeting_header:
Date: 2025-09-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Darius Patel (Redwood SE), Olga Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Head of ML, Foxden), Ethan Cole (Infra Lead, Foxden), Samira Ortiz (CISO, Foxden), Marcus Lee (Product)
summary: Discovery focused on cost/unit economics for a pilot across hosted vs dedicated vs private. Major themes: batching and cache impact on per-token cost, residency/data controls, latency SLOs for customer facing features, pilot budget constraints and benchmarking plan. Customer worried about peak latency during 99th pct and how batching affects user-perceived latency. Security/CISO asked for SOC2, KMS, and VPC integration details. Agreed next steps for pilot pricing and benchmark run.
topics: 1) Current stack and constraints 2) Target throughput/latency 3) Unit cost levers (batching, KV cache, quantization) 4) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs 5) Compliance/residency needs 6) Pilot scope and success metrics
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate the time. Quick intros?
[00:00:08] Priya (Foxden): Hi I'm Priya, head of ML at Foxden, we run parcel ETA models and want to add LLM-based routing assistant and a post-delivery summarizer.
[00:00:15] Marcus (Foxden Product): Marcus, product, thinking about customer-facing chat summarization.
[00:00:19] Ethan (Foxden Infra): Ethan, infra lead. Mainly here for cost, networking questions.
[00:00:23] Samira (Foxden CISO): Samira, security. I'll be skimming compliance items.
[00:00:26] Darius (Redwood SE): Darius, SE, I'll cover perf and batching specifics.
[00:00:30] Maya: Great. High level — you're evaluating hosted, dedicated, or private deployment for inference. Today we want to understand your traffic shape and budget constraints so we can recommend a pilot.
[00:00:45] Priya: Exactly. Our baseline traffic for the routing assistant is about 150k requests/day with an average prompt+response length in the 350-800 token range. Peaks up to 400 reqs/sec during morning windows. Budget is tight — we'd like to keep unit cost under something that scales.
[00:01:04] Darius: Okay so two levers: model choice and runtime settings. Batching and KV caching are the main cost reducers. But batching increases effective latency unless we tune thresholds and continuous batching.
[00:01:18] Ethan: When you say KV caching, you mean prefix/key-value cache for repeated context, right? We've got a lot of repeated context for the same delivery routes.
[00:01:25] Darius: Yep, KV cache — sorry sometimes docs say KV cash in speech — essentially the model's key-value attention cache we can persist across short sessions to avoid recomputing tokens. For your use-case there's a high reuse fraction so it's a big win.
[00:01:38] Priya: Quantitatively, what's the percent saving we should expect? Even a sketch is fine.
[00:01:43] Darius: Ballpark: with good prefix reuse and cache hit rates 60-80%, you can see 30-60% per-token cost reduction. With batching alone, depending on seq lengths, another 20-40% on GPU-backed serving. Combined, maybe 50-70% lower than naive single-token-per-request runs. But that depends on tail latency tolerances.
[00:02:02] Marcus: Tail latency — our SLO is 450ms p95 for interactive features. If batching raises p95 above that users will notice.
[00:02:09] Maya: Right. So tradeoff is latency vs cost. Hosted mode gives you immediate access to batching and caching suggestions and we can tune continuous batching to keep p95 under your SLO. Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk and predictable throughput, and Private gives you residency and VPC controls but has higher ops overhead.
[00:02:27] Samira: On Private — we need to know encryption in transit and at rest, KMS integrations (HSM), and audit logs. Is SOC2 in scope for hosted?
[00:02:35] Maya: Yes, hosted Redwood has SOC2 Type II. We integrate with common KMS providers — we have a managed option and also support customer-managed keys for private. Audit logs and per-token tracing are available in the Console.
[00:02:46] Samira: Good. Also want SAML SSO, RBAC, and retention controls. We cannot keep any PII beyond 30 days for this workload.
[00:02:54] Olga (Redwood SE): We can set up retention policies and redaction pipelines for logs; or configure no-persist modes in private deployments. SAML is supported for the console and RBAC can be scoped to teams.
[00:03:06] Ethan: Back to cost — you mentioned continuous batching. How do you avoid batch-wait latency for single, low-volume requests?
[00:03:13] Darius: We use a latency-aware batching policy — small time windows and adaptive thresholds. For interactive single users we keep batch latency under ~40ms by setting max-wait timers and prioritizing small batches. For background bulk ops we allow larger batch windows to maximize throughput.
[00:03:28] Priya: If we go dedicated, is there a predictable per-token price? Or do we still pay unit costs?
[00:03:34] Maya: Dedicated is committed capacity — effectively a monthly reservation. You'll pay for the capacity slot and then there's a per-token usage layer for burst or overage depending on the contract. For pilots we often provision a small dedicated pool to validate throughput then scale.
[00:03:50] Marcus: Our budget for pilot is about $12k for 4 weeks. We need to understand if that's enough for a credible test with your medium-sized model.
[00:03:58] Darius: With $12k and your traffic profile, a hosted pilot using batching+KV cache can simulate production-like costs. If you need strict residency or to measure noise-free latency, a short dedicated run for a week would consume a chunk of that. We'll model both.
[00:04:13] Priya: Can you run a bench for both hosted and dedicated with our token distribution?
[00:04:17] Darius: Yes — we ask you to provide token-length histogram and request-rate timeline. We'll run a perf job measuring p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1k-tokens with different batch sizes and cache configs.
[00:04:29] Ethan: How do fallbacks and multi-model routing work? If we prefer a light model at the tail to reduce cost, can Redwood route automatically?
[00:04:36] Maya: Yes — Smart routing will send requests to preferred model variants by policy. You can do latency-first for low token sequences and cost-first for async jobs. We also support automatic fallback to smaller models when dedicated capacity is saturated.
[00:04:47] Samira: A question on auditability — does per-token tracing expose prompt content in logs? We need to ensure PII isn't leaked to logs.
[00:04:54] Olga: Logs can be redacted or suppressed; we offer metadata-only traces and token-level cost accounting without storing user prompt text. For SOC2 we can provide details in the security packet.
[00:05:06] Priya: A bit concerned about the percieved complexity. If batching and cache configs are fiddly, who's responsible for tuning?
[00:05:12] Darius: Redwood Optimize provides recommendations automatically based on observed traffic. For pilots our SE will help tune thresholds and batching. Over time, the system learns and recommends quantization or model variants.
[00:05:24] Marcus: About quantization — do you support int8 or more aggressive Q4 variants? Any quality regressions we should expect?
[00:05:29] Darius: We support several quantization profiles. Q4 or int8 can dramatically reduce memory and cost with small quality impacts — depends on your task. We'll run evals on your prompt sets to measure regressions; we surface the delta in the Console.
[00:05:41] Ethan: Networking — if we go Private in our VPC, do we need to open outbound egress to Redwood, or is it a peering setup?
[00:05:47] Maya: Private can be either VPC peering or onsite on-prem package. For VPC we do peering and customer-managed networking — no broad egress to the public internet required — we support strict ACLs and private endpoints.
[00:06:00] Samira: Does private require an on-call ops team from our side?
[00:06:04] Maya: We have options — fully managed Private where Redwood runs the control plane with minimal hands-on required, or self-managed on-prem which will need your ops. For regulated workloads we often do a hybrid where we manage the runtime but keys and audit logs stay with the customer.
[00:06:18] Priya: Ok what's the success criteria for the pilot? What should we measure?
[00:06:21] Darius: Agree on: 1) p95 < 450ms for interactive flows 2) per-token effective cost under X (we'll propose) 3) cache hit rate > 60% for route context 4) minimal quality delta for quantized model < 2-3% on your evaluation prompts.
[00:06:38] Marcus: For pricing, will you give a per-token hosted rate and an equivalent effective per-token for dedicated?
[00:06:44] Maya: Yes — we'll send two modeled price sheets: hosted per-token tiers, and a dedicated reservation example that amortizes hardware and gives effective per-token based on your projected throughput. We'll include a sensitivity table for different batch and cache assumptions.
[00:06:57] Priya: Any gotchas on billing granularity? Do you round tokens or do subtokens matter?
[00:07:02] Maya: We bill per token with internal tokenization. We publish tokenization details and sample reconstructions; for costs we show tokens per request averaged over the sample traces you send.
[00:07:12] Ethan: One more — what's the quickest way to prove it without blowing the pilot budget?
[00:07:16] Darius: Start with hosted with caching enabled and simulated peak load tests. That gets you real p95/p99 numbers fast. If the tail looks noisy, do a short dedicated slice for peak windows.
[00:07:27] Samira: Security packet and SOC2 please.
[00:07:30] Maya: We'll attach the security packet in the follow up.
[00:07:33] Priya: Great. Also can you include an example of cache hit vs miss cost delta?
[00:07:36] Darius: Yes will include a worked example based on your token histogram.
[00:07:40] Maya: Quick recap: Redwood to send pilot pricing, sample perf configs; SE to run bench after customer shares token histogram and hourly traffic; Customer to share compliance list and retention constraints. Any other items?
[00:07:53] Marcus: No, that's it.
[00:07:55] Samira: I'll add the compliance doc to the shared folder.
[00:07:58] Maya: Perfect — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pricing and schedule.
[00:08:02] END
notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts (KV cash, SAM l). Discussed concrete pilot constraints: $12k budget, 4-week pilot, target p95 450ms. Agreed data sharing needed: token histogram, traffic timeline, compliance list.
